issues.title: release(v0.14.0): cut ladder epoch L4 and roll the seed to weekly-2026-w32
issues.body:
Build `0.13.2 -> 0.14.0`. Ladder epoch `3 -> 4`. Featured seed
`weekly-2026-w31 -> weekly-2026-w32`. **This forks the public leaderboard.**

## Why the ladder must fork

67 commits sit between `v0.13.2` and `1795cd12`. `ladder_version.txt` was last
modified in `9abe20a7`, an ancestor of `v0.13.2`, so none of those 67 bumped it.
Among them is `8791ba47` (#1137), which retimed the historical event deck to
one-turn-one-month and applied the ruled promotions -- modifying
`godot/data/events/balancing/rarity_curves.json`.

`docs/game-design/BUILD_VS_LADDER_VERSION_SPLIT.md` section 3.1 names "anything
that changes which events fire on a given seed" and "event probabilities" as
explicit BUMP triggers. Checklist questions 2, 3 and 5 are all yes.

Left at L3, main would accept runs onto a board built under different event
probabilities. Existing L3 entries stay valid and visible under L3; new runs land
on L4.

## Verified by execution, not by reading

A throwaway GUT probe run headless against this tree (then deleted):

```
PROBE CURRENT_VERSION=0.14.0
PROBE LADDER_VERSION=4
PROBE get_board_version()=L4
PROBE get_weekly_seed()=weekly-2026-w32
```

`python tools/sync_version.py --check` reports zero drift.

## Tests

**Fast gate, measured both sides, identical:**

| | tests | failures | files |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1212 | 0 | 119/119 |
| after | 1212 | 0 | 119/119 |

Worth saying plainly: that identity means **no test asserted the old epoch or the
old version**. Nothing guarded the value this PR changes. The green is real, but
it is not evidence about this change.

**Simulation tier: NOT verified locally.** It times out at the hardcoded 900s
reporting `0 tests, 0 fail`. Unmodified `origin/main` reproduces that identically
(run three times, ~15 min each), so this PR is exonerated by A/B rather than
excused. The tier is green in CI on Ubuntu for both the #1137 commit
(run `31091011227`) and the latest main run (`31130859770`), with `--min-tests 80`
enforced. Filed as #1168.

## Release notes were hand-written

The `[0.14.0]` CHANGELOG section was written **by hand from the 67 commits**,
every bullet tied to a merged commit. It was deliberately not assembled from
`[Unreleased]`: that path produced the v0.13.2 notes, which announce #500 as
delivered while #500 is **still open**, and pdoom1.com serves those notes live to
players. Filed as #1165 per `coordination#35`.

## Also here

- `docs/ROADMAP.md`: v0.14 row `L3 -> L4`, later rows shifted, and the
  "one Theme = one Epoch" rule marked as intent rather than invariant -- v0.13
  actually spanned L2 and L3.
- `docs/rituals/gate_5_seed_blessing.md`, `docs/RELEASE_PLATFORMS.md`: stop
  asserting a stale seed/epoch in the present tense; point at the SSOT.

## Known gap this PR does not close

`tools/check_ladder_bump.py` warns in the **wrong direction** on a correct epoch
cut -- "ladder_version.txt was bumped but NO gameplay-surface files changed" --
because an epoch cut is by construction a version-files-only commit while the
gameplay change landed in an earlier PR. It is advisory (`|| true` in CI), so
when #1137 tripped the correct warning, nothing stopped. Detailed in the report
accompanying this PR; not fixed here.

Refs #1137, #1165, #1168

issues.title: docs(postmortem): the SUNDAY capture pack for 2026-08-06/07 -- four mechanisms, not one
issues.body:
The postmortem capture pack for the 2026-08-06/07 cycle, tagged **SUNDAY** in the
filename and in a band repeated on all 17 printed pages, because Pip is filtering
the printer by that tag tonight and must be able to skip it at a glance.

It is on the printer already.

## The headline, measured

**48 pull requests merged in seven days and nothing shipped to a player.** Version
frozen at `0.13.2` since 07-29, ladder frozen at L3 since 07-27, zero changelog
entries across all 48, and the open-issue count moved **201 -> 208** while the
week's two triage lanes closed nothing they identified.

## The single-mechanism framing did not hold

The brief proposed one through-line -- *"a plausible output from a process that did
not do the work."* Tested against eleven failures, that describes the **outcome**
(nothing complained), not the generator. **Four generators, four different
remedies, and no single remedy catches more than one of them:**

| | Mechanism | Distinguishing property | Remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | The vacuous check | The instrument exists, is wired in, and the bad answer is unreachable | Show it returning the other answer |
| M2 | The absorbing empty state | No instrument involved -- the data path itself has a state indistinguishable from success | Zero is an error until proven |
| M3 | The self-referential measurement | The number is real and traceable; only its provenance claim is false | Derive from a generator, or carry a provenance flag |
| M4 | Escape mangling in a generated artefact | Looking harder does not help -- only a parser sees it | Parse the artefact before writing it |

Plus **M5**, `git reset` in the main checkout destroying in-flight work twice in 24
hours, which is not a plausible-output failure at all and is the cleanest disproof
of the single-pattern reading.

## The worst recurrence from 07-31

**"A check that cannot fail."** 07-31 FINDING 9 named it precisely -- every sync
step was `continue-on-error`, so *"the job could not reach a failed state."* Seven
days later it recurred **four times across three repos**, and one of them is the
guard covering the ladder, the exact axis 07-31's FINDING 5 was about:

- `check_ladder_bump.py` runs `|| true` in CI, so it cannot fail a build -- and its
  `GAMEPLAY_PREFIXES` exclude `godot/autoload/`, where #1137's retime lives. **It
  reported nothing on F1**, the cycle's highest-cost defect. A person writing a
  decision card found that 31 hours later.
- W6: a published `grep` whose `|` is a literal, so it returns 0 against a file
  containing all four search terms -- committed inside the comment adopting a rule
  about commands.
- The phase guard's first-draft regex, which matched nothing on the actual #1134
  line and went green.
- `certes`' `check-language.sh` (`coordination#29`), which truncated three of seven
  rules on a pipe split. `retreat.*hosting` was never checked for six months.

Naming a failure mode in a document demonstrably did not stop it recurring. Both
instances that *were* caught were caught by a practice -- prove it red, run a
control -- not by the document.

## Instruments: what earned its cost

- **Taste profile -- the clearest earn.** Its *nulls* paid: iteration bought nothing
  measurable (p=0.34), which redirected USD 13.20 of re-rolls into breadth the same
  day and killed the 08-03 "highest variant wins" convention.
- **Phase-guard audit -- earned on the hollow-guard catch alone**, despite being a
  near-null by design. Also the only instrument that states its own boundary:
  *"The scanner is green on a live bug."*
- **Guard-first practice -- cheapest, highest hit rate.** Two of the four R1
  instances were caught this way.
- **Claim-audit rule -- keep, narrow.** Real catches (two in a merged PR body, one
  already in two repos), but the two artifacts that scored *structurally* both
  predate the rule, and the rule produced M1 in its own body.
- **Triage + mining -- the pair earned it, the outcome did not happen.** Mining
  caught five wrong absorption claims that would have closed #622 and #577 silently.
  Zero issues were closed. 201 -> 208.
- **The workshop -- close to a null in the room.** Sourced to the two seats that
  filed it, not to me: *"two of the six items did not need this instrument"* and
  *"the workshop was not necessary for four of six rulings."* Keep the prep (it
  demolished three of the agenda's four premises), keep the seals, cut the agenda.

## Ceremony

Printing documents nobody acts on. The 08-06 handover's own heading: *"The three
documents produced today, all printed, none acted on."* This pack is a fourth, and
carries its own falsifier: if by 2026-08-14 none of P1-P8 has started and no issue
references it, stop producing them rather than produce a better one.

## Three brief claims did not reproduce as worded

Corrected in place, not footnoted:

1. **The `.pck` was built for playtest, not shipped.** No tag or release exists past
   `v0.13.2`; the build is labelled "explicitly not shippable."
2. **The reflog does not record reset MODE.** Two resets in the main checkout
   discarded commits that had to be recovered -- one carrying `slot_picks.json` --
   but `--hard` is asserted, not measured, and the pack says so.
3. **The changelog claim splits.** #791/#811 are stale issue state (squash-merge
   does not fire closes-keywords). **#500 is not**: the published v0.13.2 release
   body, live at pdoom1.com/game-changelog/, announces a Research Quality toggle the
   design ruling replaced.

## One new finding, measured while writing

`abd6c7d0` pushed **direct to main** and edited `godot/data/credits.json`, which
`test_credits_data.gd` asserts against. `godot-tests.yml`'s push filter covers
`godot/**/*.gd`, `*.tscn` and `project.godot` -- **not `godot/data/**`** -- and the
unfiltered `pull_request` trigger did not apply. So the honest sentence is
**"main's Godot suite is green as of `553f0b7c`"**, five commits back, not "main is
green".

## Not touched

`version.txt`, `ladder_version.txt`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `godot/`, `art_generated/`,
`tools/art_review/` -- all owned by concurrent lanes. Two files added, nothing
edited.

---

Printed: `python tools/print_doc.py tools/runsheet/SUNDAY-postmortem-2026-08-07.html`
-- 17 pages, SUNDAY band verified on every one.

Full text: `G:\Documents\Organising_Life\Code\pdoom1\docs\POSTMORTEM_2026-08-07_CAPTURE.md`

issues.title: Simulation tier cannot be run locally on Windows -- 15-min hardcoded timeout, and a timeout reports as '0 tests, 0 fail'
issues.body:
Found while cutting v0.14.0 / L4, on the one release where the simulation tier is
the tier that matters (the cut forks the ladder because #1137 retimed the event
deck, and replay/determinism is exactly what this tier guards).

## The measurement

`python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --simulation --ci-mode --min-tests 80` on the
Windows dev machine, in a clean worktree at `origin/main` (`1795cd12`):

```
[TEST] Running 'simulation' tests in res://tests/unit/simulation (8 files on disk)
[FAIL] Tests timed out after 15 minutes!
[TOTALS] simulation: 0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)
```

Run three times, ~15 min each:

| tree | stdout | result |
|---|---|---|
| v0.14.0 release branch | pipe | timeout, 0 tests |
| v0.14.0 release branch | redirected to a file | timeout, 0 tests |
| **unmodified `origin/main`** | redirected to a file | **timeout, 0 tests** |

The third row is the point: **main alone reproduces it.** The epoch cut is
exonerated by that A/B. This is pre-existing.

Meanwhile the same tier is **green in GitHub Actions on Ubuntu**, including on
the #1137 commit itself (run `31091011227`, job "Simulation Tests") and on the
latest main run (`31130859770`). The workflow passes `--min-tests 80`, so a
zero-test run would have failed the job; it did not.

## Two separate defects

**1. The tier cannot be run locally on Windows at all.**
15 minutes is hardcoded -- `scripts/run_godot_tests.py:329`,
`subprocess.run(..., timeout=900)` -- with no CLI flag to raise it. So a
developer on this machine has no way to get a result, only a timeout. Every
local run of this tier is a guaranteed 15-minute wait for nothing.

**2. A timeout reports as `0 tests` rather than as "unknown".**
`[TOTALS] simulation: 0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)` reads like a measurement. It is
not one -- no test was observed to pass or fail. This is the repo's house
failure mode (silent wrongness) wearing a green-adjacent number: "0 fail" is
literally true and completely misleading.

## Probable cause of the slowness (partially diagnosed, not proven)

Running GUT directly against `res://tests/unit/simulation` floods stdout with one
line per RNG draw:

```
[VerificationTracker] RNG: event_hist_arxiv_218ce086ce67d573=0.948207 -> 69befb4da53334e3...
```

Sampled mid-run, the Godot process had **16.2 minutes wall clock against 7.9
seconds of user CPU** -- it is blocked on I/O, not computing. The print is
`debug_mode`-gated (`godot/autoload/verification_tracker.gd:225-226`), so it is
test-only and does **not** ship to players; a sim test turns it on deliberately.

Caveat, stated because it undercuts the theory: redirecting stdout to a file
instead of a pipe did **not** fix it. So console/pipe I/O is at most part of the
story and something else is also slow or stuck. Not chased further -- a release
was in flight.

## Asks

1. Add a `--timeout` flag to `run_godot_tests.py` so the tier can at least be
   run to completion locally.
2. Make a timeout report as **UNKNOWN / DID NOT RUN**, never as `0 tests, 0 fail`.
   A gate that cannot distinguish "nothing failed" from "nothing ran" is the
   exact defect #640 fixed for the fast gate; the slow tier still has it.
3. Find the real Windows slowness. Start by checking whether the per-RNG-draw
   debug print can be buffered or suppressed under GUT, then bisect the 8 files
   in `godot/tests/unit/simulation/` for the one that dominates.

## Consequence accepted for v0.14.0

v0.14.0 shipped with the simulation tier verified **only in CI**, not locally,
with that stated plainly in the handover rather than smoothed over. The fast gate
was green locally both before and after the change (1212 tests, 0 failures,
119/119 files -- identical counts).

issues.title: art(l2): bridge the review state to the runner and fire the L2 wave -- 306 images, USD 15.30
issues.body:
The L2 wave of the 2026-08-07 art night ran. 306 images, USD 15.30 from the
ledger, zero failures. This PR is the code and data that made it possible plus
the two prompt fixes it exposed; the images themselves are under
`art_generated/`, which is gitignored in full.

## What `--picks` actually wanted

`run_art_night.py --picks tools/art_review/review_state.json` returned
`[ABORT] L2 needs picks and none parsed`. Two independent mismatches, and
neither one raised anything:

1. **Shape.** `load_picks`' dict branch expects `{id: [tag, tag]}` -- a list of
   tag strings per id. `review_state.json` stores
   `{id: {"verdict":..., "tags":[], "note":..., "updated_at":...}}`. Iterating
   that value yields the field names `verdict`/`tags`/`note`/`updated_at`, none
   of which are in `FAVOURABLE_TAGS`, so all 5794 entries read as
   non-favourable. Not a crash -- a shrug.
2. **Vocabulary.** `FAVOURABLE_TAGS` is
   `{love, like, promote, favour, favor, hero, yes, keep}`. `iterate` is not in
   it, and `iterate` is exactly the verdict L2 exists to consume.

**Bridge:** `load_picks` accepts a second shape -- a flat JSON list of ids,
taken verbatim with no tag filtering. New `tools/art_review/export_picks.py`
emits that. Verdict policy therefore lives in the review layer where it is
readable and arguable, instead of widening the runner's tag vocabulary and
quietly making `keep` mean "vary this".

## Which picks, and what was excluded

Fed: the **51** parseable `iterate` verdicts on the `an0807` batch.

| bucket | n | fed? | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `an0807` iterate, scene cells | 51 | yes | "this direction is right, vary it" -- literally L2's input |
| `an0807` iterate, L0 swatch sheets | 5 | no | cell key is a bare palette id (`p01`); no subject/rendering/palette triple to vary. Dropped **and printed**. |
| `an0807` keep | 143 | no | a keep says "this image is good", not "vary this". That is an L3 signal. |
| iterate on pre-art-night batches | 70 | no | filenames are not art-night cells; `load_picks` cannot resolve them at all |
| all keeps corpus-wide | 3837 | no | 3837 x 6 steps x USD 0.05 = USD 1151, roughly 15x the whole ceiling |

`picks_target` raised **36 -> 51**. At 36 the runner would have silently thrown
away 15 of Pip's verdicts. It is also the difference between clearing the run's
own underspend floor and not:

| picks | L2 USD | run after L3 | vs floor 68.00 | headroom left |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 36 (old) | 10.80 | 66.25 | **missed** -- needs a topup wave | 9.25 |
| 51 (this) | 15.30 | 70.75 | met | 4.75 |

## Fixes this exposed

- **`load_picks` truncation is no longer silent.** It now prints when
  `picks_target` drops picks. Same class of wrongness as the tag bug.
- **Text leak, one mechanical cause found.** `poster_props` literally requested
  lettering: *"keyboards with worn legends"* -- legends are the printed
  characters on keycaps. Now blank keycaps. `poster_base`'s no-text clause also
  names the objects that really carry printing (binder spines, whiteboards,
  warning plates, rubber stamps, cartons, screens, keycaps) and offers a
  non-letterform fallback. Both clauses sit at the same prompt position and are
  constant across all 6 steps of a pick, so the within-pick axis comparison is
  unaffected. Only an L1-to-L2 comparison is contaminated, and generation
  lineage is a measured null.
- **`apply_review.py` Hold entries for the 7 L2 batches.** Without them
  `build_full_gallery.py` refuses to build -- correctly, since a review pass
  would strand its own keeps.

## Result, read from the ledger not the plan

- 306 ok / 0 failed / 0 stopped at ceiling, USD 15.30
- run total **USD 46.75 of 75.50**; **USD 28.75 left** against L3's USD 24.00
- 306 masters, 306 provenance sidecars, each with prompt sha256, model, size,
  quality, tariff cost, UTC timestamp, taste-brief sha256 (spot-checked, not
  assumed)
- axis coverage 48/48/42/42/42/42/42 across yaw, pitch, distance, title space,
  decay, quiet, style tween
- gallery rebuilt: 61 batches, 6511 assets; the `node --check` gate reported
  method `node --check`, so it genuinely parsed rather than falling back to the
  regex scanner

**What would prove this wrong:** tariff dollars are the published price, not
billed truth. Reconcile against the OpenAI billing dashboard before quoting the
spend anywhere it matters.

Follow-on to #1158.

issues.title: docs(chronicle): the two days, timestamped -- every cell reducible to a command, nine marked unknown
issues.body:
Pip asked for the record itself -- *"timestamp all this, marvellous data."* So the deliverable here is the accuracy of the TIME, not the story.

Written under the `coordination#31` headline rule this seat adopted at `2026-08-06T10:55:41Z`: a claim in a title, summary line, table cell or bolded sentence must be reducible to a command another party can run. A chronicle is nothing but table cells, so it is the hardest test that rule has had. **No time in it came from a PR body, an agent report or a session summary.** Section 7 lists every command used, so another party can rebuild the tables from scratch.

## Timezone, verified rather than asserted

All UTC sources shifted by `+10:00`. Checked against the one local time recorded independently: `docs/SEAT_VOICE.md` has the voice grant at **19:24 AEST / 09:24 UTC**, and `09:24 + 10:00 = 19:24`. Second check, machine-side: the `#31` comment whose body says *"~20:15 AEST"* has `createdAt 10:12:12Z` -> 20:12 AEST, three minutes early, which is the expected sign. A ten-hour error would have read 10:12.

## What it covers

- **Span 2026-08-06 07:47:27 AEST to the snapshot at 2026-08-07 18:05:15 AEST -- 1 d 10 h 17 m 48 s.** The L3 art wave was **still running** at snapshot, so the ledger was copied first and the L3 figures are labelled a floor, not a total.
- **21 PRs merged, all squash-merged** (`%aI == %cI` on every one, which never happens on hand-authored work), so `mergedAt` is used for landing time and `%aI` only as a blame proxy. Longest open 18 h 01 m (#1158); shortest 3 min (#1159). **No release** -- newest tag is still `v0.13.2` from 2026-07-31.
- **The workshop to the second**: seal 18:32:19, opened 20:02:49 (1 h 30 m 30 s later), three ballots inside 31 m 42 s, minute 22:31:56.
- **The money, from `ledger.jsonl`**: 974 rows, all `ok`, all `attempt: 1` -- zero retries across the run. L0+L1 = 652 images / USD 31.448 in 47 m 49 s; L2 = 306 / USD 15.30 in 25 m. 17 h 16 m idle between L1 and L2, waiting on picks rather than capacity. Every USD figure is flagged **tariff, not billed**, because the run log flags it.

## Introduction-to-discovery, which nobody had computed

Six defects blamed to the commit that introduced them.

| Defect | Gap |
|---|---|
| Six `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG headings | 369 d 19 h 17 m |
| `quality` never passed to `images.generate` | 241 d 12 h 32 m |
| F3 event injection permalocks the run | 224 d 17 h 41 m |
| `take_loan` defined twice | 24 d 04 h 30 m |
| Gallery keyboard dead | 3 d 01 h 36 m |
| `--picks` shape mismatch | <= 0 h 59 m |

The 369 d headline carries a caveat in the body: an `[Unreleased]` heading is not wrong when it is written, only at the release cut that fails to rename it, and **that cut is not dated here**. So the longest unambiguous gap is the `quality` parameter -- 241 d from writing the call to writing it down in a manifest note, then a further **385 d** from writing it down to fixing it today.

The gallery's dead keyboard is only 3 days, but it is the more interesting shape: one literal newline inside a JS string, a hard `SyntaxError` that killed every key binding, surviving three days because nobody opened the page and no test could have caught it -- the tool ships a scripted DOM harness that structurally cannot detect "the keyboard does not work".

## What it refuses to say

The brief asserted two `git reset --hard` incidents destroyed in-flight work. **The reflog shows four resets** in the main checkout (16:17:01, 22:22:40, 22:26:32, 09:22:39) **and does not record the mode** -- `--hard`, `--mixed` and `--soft` write the same line. So the four times are given and the `--hard` claim is not made.

**Nine cells are marked unknown and enumerated in 6.5** so the count is checkable.

**Two sources disagree, both shown:**
1. `c743710b`'s author and committer dates differ by 11 h. Committer trusted, corroborated by the reflog landing 2 m 39 s later and `SEAT_VOICE.md`'s mtime one second before that.
2. `pdoom-data`'s addendum says *"posted before the seal opens"* but carries a `createdAt` **88 seconds after** the seal opened. `createdAt` trusted; the hash it cites was not checked, so the discrepancy stands recorded rather than explained away.

Section 6.6 records this seat's own **6-wrong-in-68** rate from `docs/CLAIM_AUDIT_2026-08-06.md` as the base rate a reader should apply to this document, which has not itself been audited.

## No generator

No `tools/build_chronicle.py`. The ordering, the trust decisions in section 6 and the caveats in section 5 are the whole value and none of them are derivable, so a generator would have run exactly once. The one part that **is** mechanical -- the ledger aggregation -- is quoted in full in section 7 instead.

## Files

- `docs/CHRONICLE_2026-08-06_07.md`
- `tools/runsheet/chronicle-2026-08-06_07.html` -- print edition, house A4 style, 12.5pt floor, ASCII chrome, legible in black and white. **Not printed** -- Pip is out.

Touches nothing under `godot/`, and does not touch `version.txt`, `ladder_version.txt` or `CHANGELOG.md` -- the v0.14.0 lane is cutting concurrently.

`G:\Documents\Organising_Life\Code\pdoom1\tools\runsheet\chronicle-2026-08-06_07.html` (after merge; on this branch it is at `G:\Documents\Organising_Life\Code\pdoom1\.claude\worktrees\chronicle\tools\runsheet\chronicle-2026-08-06_07.html`)

issues.title: feat(art): a share set -- the missing route from "Pip likes it" to a public surface (126 candidates, 6.3% text-leak measured)
issues.body:
## The question

Pip, after applying 262 verdicts to the `an0807` art night: *"There are a shit
load of art assets I just judged, let's also figure out who owns me promoting
them up so we can social media / website them in the announcement run?"*

## Ownership -- verified, and it holds

- **Into the game:** ADR-0019. Generated -> Library -> Packed, and the only path
  into `godot/assets/` is a mechanically verified demand entry. pdoom1 owns it.
- **Onto a public surface:** `coordination#31` A2 bit 3, **`pdoom1-website` owns
  `publishable`**. Confirmed against both pdoom1's Phase 3 ballot ("pdoom1 does
  not want it and should not be given it. The website offered; take the offer")
  and the recorder's minute ("**SURVIVED.** Ruled. Pip: yes, build it"). Nothing
  here takes that gate back.

**One correction to the framing I was handed:** ADR-0019 does not use
`promotable/contested/held/blocked` -- those are `#1107`'s vocabulary. The ADR's
states are Generated / Library / Packed, plus "packed-but-undemanded" discovered
by measurement. It mentions publication, the website, and public surfaces **not
once**. That is not an oversight in the ADR; it is the gap.

## The gap, confirmed

ADR-0019 routes art that a **game slot** demands. An asset Pip likes that no slot
needs is never packed, so **there is nothing for the website to pull** -- it has
no route to a public surface at all. On this run that is *all 143 of his keeps*.
The website cannot exercise a gate over an empty set.

## What this adds

A **share set**: a tracked declaration of Library art pdoom1 offers for public
use, derived from verdicts already applied. Pip does not review anything twice.

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `docs/copy/ART_SHARE_SET.md` | the human doc -- read this first |
| `docs/copy/art_share_set.json` | the manifest the website pulls (143 entries) |
| `docs/copy/art_share_set_prompts.json` | `prompt_sha256` -> full prompt body |
| `tools/assets/build_share_set.py` | the generator (`--check`, `--html`, `--stage`) |
| `tools/art_review/scan_text_leak.py` | the OCR text gate |
| `tools/art_review/text_scan_art_night_2026-08-07.json` | its output, the evidence |

It lives in `docs/copy/` because that folder is the ACTIVE POLICY seam: the
website reads the game, never the reverse. `README.md` gains it as a seam entry,
so the website seat learns of it by reading the contract rather than by being
told. The website never touches `review_state.json`, which stays a pdoom1
internal.

## What qualifies, and the arguments

`keep` is **necessary, not sufficient**. `serve_review.py` defines it as "accept
it" -- taste, and only taste. ADR-0019 agrees from the other end: "Verdicts still
gate Library admission (taste)... none of them implies packing."

- **`iterate` excluded (56).** Not on a rule -- on his own words. Every note he
  left on an `iterate` in this run is a complaint (*"slightly too washed out,
  composition feels odd"*, *"this composition feels weird"*, *"slightyl too
  crisp"*), and every note he left on a `keep` is praise. `iterate` is defined as
  "on-brief but not final". Publishing one publishes an image he already called
  wrong.
- **`discard` excluded (63).**
- **Unjudged excluded (390 of 652)**, including all of `l1_grid` (220) and
  `l0_anchors` (54). Unjudged is not a quiet yes. Note `l1_grid` was described to
  me as a hero-shaped batch -- it is 1536x1024, but it carries **zero verdicts**,
  so it cannot enter.
- **Older Library assets excluded, structurally.** The builder cannot emit an
  entry without a run-ledger line and a `.meta.json` sidecar. An unattributable
  asset therefore *cannot* enter -- a mechanism, not a policy anyone must
  remember. `ASSET_PROVENANCE_SCOPE_2026-08-06` is why: 96.3% attributable by
  class, but 31.6% of packed assets have their only evidence in a gitignored
  single-copy directory and 6 are unattributable outright. That cannot back a
  public claim. Widening needs the `coordination#32` backfill first.

## Tiers -- because the consumer wants images to look at

143 entries, **126 publication candidates**:

| tier | n | |
|---|---:|---|
| `hero` | 5 | `keep` AND he typed praise -- *"love this"*, *"love this one"*, *"touch of green is nice"*, *"nice and warm"*, *"Nice altar, good stylishness"* |
| `feature` | 121 | `keep`, text-clean scene, no note either way |
| `reference` | 8 | `keep`, but colour swatch sheets. **Not candidates** -- labelled rather than dropped in front of the website seat unexplained |
| `quarantine_text` | 9 | `keep`, but OCR found lettering |

The `hero` rule leans on a measured property of *these 262 verdicts* -- notes on
keeps are praise, notes on iterates are reservations -- not a general law. The
note text ships in every entry so a reader can check that rather than take it.

## Text leak: measured, 6.3% of keeps

The run banned text in every prompt. It leaked.

RapidOCR (CPU, offline) over all 262 judged masters -- **17 carry a detection, 14
at confidence >= 0.60. Among the 143 keeps, 9. A 6.3% leak rate.**

Validated before trusting: fires on the known positive `s17_f01` ("DESICCANT",
conf 0.89), silent on two known-clean images.

The worst are not garbled, which is the point -- `'Plan A'` / `'Plan B'` /
`'Final Decision'` at 0.85 on a whiteboard, `'PENDING'` / `'APPROVED'` /
`'REJECTED'` at 0.83-0.88 on a status board. Some are garbled, which is worse in
public: `'PENDOVED'`, `'PPROVED'`, `'Nex+ Steps'`, `'De Bg aat'`.

**Ten of the seventeen are subject `s07`**, one recurring status-board scene. The
leak concentrates in prompts describing a surface a real room would letter -- so
the fix is that subject, not the pipeline.

**Any detection quarantines**, not just a confident one: a false quarantine costs
one image in 130, a false pass puts a garbled word on an image chosen precisely
for being prominent. Confidences travel with the entry so a borderline call can
be overruled on the evidence.

**Honest limit: this is a LOWER BOUND.** OCR misses small, low-contrast and
stylised lettering. A clean scan is evidence of absence, not proof of it. And
`s17_f01` -- the one leak found by eye -- is in the *unjudged* remainder, so
leakage is not confined to what he reviewed.

## Provenance, and the limit it cannot clear

Every entry carries `origin: generated_model`, model, backend, `run_id`,
`job_id`, `prompt_sha256`, UTC timestamp, quality, tariff cost. Full prompt
bodies ship **in git**, so "machine-generated, this model, this prompt" is
substantiable from a fresh clone rather than from a gitignored sidecar -- which
is exactly the weakness the provenance pass found in the older material.
Rebuilding that failure would have been the `coordination#15` shape.

**The API exposes no seed.** `seed: null` with a note in every entry. The record
establishes *what was asked for*, not how to reproduce the output. Public copy
should say "generated with this model from this prompt", never "reproducible".
Cost figures are tariff arithmetic (`cost_is_billed_truth: false`).

## Surfaces

Per entry, derived from pixel size rather than asserted. **Web and social: yes**,
at any normal display size. **Print at poster size: no, for every entry.** 1536px
long edge is ~5.1in at 300dpi and this pipeline has no upscale path. A poster
needs a regenerated source, not a resample.

## No bytes in git

The manifest carries paths. The 126 candidates are ~354MB, `ART_MASTERS_POLICY`
forbids art over 1MB in git, and the masters bucket is deliberately non-public
("NON-public (auth-only, not a web path)") -- so there is no surface the website
can fetch from today. Bridging that is a deliberate handover and Pip's call, not
something a build script should do quietly. `--stage DIR` prepares it off-git;
already run to `G:\tmp\pdoom1-art-masters\share_set_2026-08-07`.

## What this cannot offer, said plainly

Every candidate is an **L1** image: `medium` quality, one variant per cell, from
an unattended wide-net wave. **L2 and L3 are unrun** -- they need a picks file,
and ~USD 35 of the funded budget is unspent. L3 is the level whose entire purpose
is few, large, `high`-quality heroes.

So: 126 competent images Pip liked, fine for web and social, **none of them made
to be a hero**. The right answer to "the website wants beautiful things" is
generating better ones with the headroom that exists, not widening this set. That
is Pip's spend decision; this PR exists so he can make it knowing exactly what
the free alternative already contains.

## Two silent-wrongness bugs found while building this

1. A missing text scan made the builder emit an **ungated** manifest with 9 extra
   "candidates" and say nothing -- indistinguishable from a gated one. Now a hard
   error, with an explicit `--no-text-scan` that stamps the manifest as ungated.
2. Flat staging by basename **collided**: `l1_palette` and `l1_probe` both contain
   cell `s01_r01_p01`, from *different models* (gpt-image-1.5 vs gpt-image-2), and
   one silently overwrote the other. Staged names now carry the block, and
   uniqueness is asserted rather than assumed.

## The separate commit you should look at first

`chore(art-review)` commits `review_state.json`, which was **uncommitted in the
main checkout** -- 3,081 added verdicts including all 262 from this run, plus a
week of pixellab verdicts. It is the only copy, and this repo has lost in-flight
work to `git reset --hard` in the main checkout twice in 24 hours. Kept as its
own commit so it can be reverted independently.

**If your working copy of that file is dirty when you pull: KEEP YOURS** (it is
newer and a superset), then re-run `python tools/assets/build_share_set.py`.

## Open to disagreement

- `reference` (swatch sheets) could just be omitted rather than labelled. I kept
  them so the website seat is told what they are instead of inferring it.
- The `hero` rule is 5 assets resting on 5 notes. If Pip disagrees with any of
  them the tier is wrong by 20%.
- Quarantining on any detection will hold back some images whose "text" is
  texture. That is the deliberate trade; the evidence to overturn it is in the
  entry.

Open: `G:\Documents\Organising_Life\Code\pdoom1\art_generated\share_set.html`

Not wired into pre-commit: `build_share_set.py --check` needs `art_generated/`,
which is gitignored, so it cannot run in CI or on a fresh clone. Run it by hand
after touching verdicts.

Nothing was moved, deleted, or promoted into `godot/`.

issues.title: CHANGELOG.md can announce open issues as shipped -- six [Unreleased] headings + stray 2025 content inside the [0.13.2] section
issues.body:
Raised from `coordination#35` (pdoom1-website seat, 2026-08-07 16:52) and verified
independently while cutting v0.14.0 / L4.

## The defect that already shipped

The **v0.13.2 release body announced work that had not landed in v0.13.2**:

| announced | issue | actual state |
|---|---|---|
| Scenario/Mod Hook System | #483 | closed 2025-12-13, ~7.5 months before it was announced |
| Research Quality System | #500 | **STILL OPEN** |
| Python 3.11 baseline | #527 | closed same day it was filed, 2026-06-26 |

Current issue numbers are #1150+. The release announced work from the #483-#527 band.

This reaches players with no human in between: pdoom1.com `/game-changelog/`
renders release bodies fetched live from the releases API. Right now it tells
players that #500 is delivered while #500 is open.

## Two distinct mechanisms, both verified in `CHANGELOG.md` at `1795cd12`

**Mechanism A -- stray legacy content INSIDE a released section.**
This is the one that actually produced the v0.13.2 body. The `## [0.13.2]`
section spans lines 9-114. At line 76 there is a bare `---`, and lines 78-111
then carry `### Added` / `### Fixed` / `### Technical` blocks describing #483,
#500, #527 -- 2025-era content sitting under a 2026-07-31 heading. Anything that
slices "the newest version section" picks it up and is not wrong to do so; the
file says that content belongs to 0.13.2.

**Mechanism B -- six `## [Unreleased]` headings.**
Lines 7, 468, 546, 807, 1174, 1344. Three carry 2025-09 dates
(`- 2025-09-17 'RNG Architecture Discovery Release'`,
`- 2025-09-19 'Bug Sweep Session'`, plus an undated
`'Input System Architecture Overhaul'`). Any tool that greps for
`^## \[Unreleased\]` and takes a match other than the first, or takes all
matches, assembles years of accumulated text. The top one (line 7) is currently
empty, so B was *not* the v0.13.2 mechanism -- but it is live and will bite a
different tool.

## Deliberately NOT fixed in v0.14.0

Ruled by the pdoom1 seat under Pip's standing delegation: not worth doing at
speed on a Friday evening with a release in flight. The v0.14.0 release body was
instead hand-written from the 67 commits between `v0.13.2` and `1795cd12`, with
every bullet tied to a merged commit. The stray 0.13.2 block was left in place.

## Asks for next cycle

1. Repair `CHANGELOG.md`: one `[Unreleased]` heading; re-file the lines 78-111
   block under whichever real version shipped it (#483/#500/#527 suggest the
   v0.11-v0.12 band, and #500 should not be claimed at all until it closes).
2. Make CHANGELOG hygiene a release **BLOCKER** -- the website seat asked for
   this and the pdoom1 seat ruled YES for next cycle. A mechanical check is
   cheap: exactly one `[Unreleased]`, every heading below it a valid semver with
   a date, monotonically decreasing.
3. Correct the live v0.13.2 release body via `gh release edit`, since it is
   currently being served to players.

## Related

- `coordination#35`
- #500 (announced as delivered, still open)

issues.title: godot/data/historical_events.json carries two mojibake titles; the upstream repair cannot reach a hand-carried copy
issues.body:
**The shipped event snapshot carries two mojibake titles.**

Filed by the `pdoom-data` seat. Measured on `Bort` at 2026-08-07 17:0x AEST, twice: once by an independent scan, then again by hand before filing.

*(Rewritten 17:2x -- the first version of this body was mechanically derived from the sibling report filed as `pdoom1-website#282` and carried phrasing that belonged to that repo. This is the pdoom1-specific version.)*

## The finding

`godot/data/historical_events.json`, the 1,194-record snapshot taken from `pdoom-data`:

    uk_ai_safety_to_security_2025
      is        : 'UK AI Safety Institute \xe2†’ AI Security Institute'
      should be : 'UK AI Safety Institute -> AI Security Institute'

    us_aisi_to_caisi_2025
      is        : 'US AISI \xe2†’ Center for AI Standards and Innovation'
      should be : 'US AISI -> Center for AI Standards and Innovation'

`\xe2†’` is the bytes `E2 86 92` -- `U+2192` RIGHTWARDS ARROW in UTF-8 -- read as CP1252. Single-level mangling; the recovered strings contain nothing further suspicious.

Whether a player sees these depends on whether either event surfaces in play, which is a pdoom1 question rather than a pdoom-data one.

## Use `->`, not the recovered arrow

Upstream `pdoom-data` repaired these on 2026-08-06 to the ASCII `->`, because that repo is ASCII-only and its repair rule is an explicit substitution map that errors on unmapped characters rather than guessing. Writing back the reconstructed `U+2192` would leave the copies disagreeing in a **new** way rather than the old one. Verified upstream on `main`:

    'UK AI Safety Institute -> AI Security Institute'

## Why the upstream fix did not reach you

`pdoom-data` shipped a transcoding gate today (`pdoom-data#69`). It scans every JSON and JSONL under its own `data/` tree, and **it cannot see this file by construction** -- `godot/data/historical_events.json` is a frozen hand-carried copy that does not regenerate, which is exactly why the 08-06 repair did not propagate.

So the gate protects the source and not the consumer. This seat has no standing to choose pdoom1's answer, but the two available shapes are: the snapshot becomes a **refreshed artifact** with a recorded provenance and a re-sync step, or pdoom1 runs its **own** transcoding check over `godot/data/` in CI. They are not exclusive, and only the first stops it recurring.

Detection rule if you want it standalone -- and deliberately reimplement rather than import, so that a defect in one implementation is not invisible to both:

> a string is corrupt if it contains `U+00C2`, `U+00C3` or `U+00E2` **and** `s.encode('cp1252').decode('utf-8')` succeeds and differs. The result is what it should have been.

Two traps, both of which cost this seat time today: split JSONL on `\n` only, because `str.splitlines()` also breaks on `U+2028` and `U+0085`, which occur inside string values in these corpora and will fragment records into false findings; and print findings `ascii()`-escaped, because a Windows console re-mangles mojibake on output and a genuinely corrupt string can print back looking correct.

## Scope, measured rather than assumed

A cross-repo sweep today scanned 536 files in `pdoom1` (`godot/data/` and `docs/`), 347 in `pdoom1-website`, and 68 markdown files in `coordination`. **Every file on disk decoded cleanly as UTF-8**; the corruption is inside string values, not in file encoding. Findings were exactly these two records, in this file and in `pdoom1-website/public/data/events.json` (filed as `pdoom1-website#282`). `pdoom1/docs/` is clean. `coordination` is clean.

## Related

`pdoom-data#68` (the finding), `pdoom-data#69` (the gate), `pdoom-data#52` (the missing producer that surfaced it), `pdoom1-website#282` (the same two records in the site's served copy), `coordination#10` (the transcoding species).

issues.title: Review: what does pdoom1 actually want from pdoom-data? (measured inventory, no proposal)
issues.body:
**Raised at Pip's direction** (`pdoom-data#55`): pdoom1 decides what it wants from pdoom-data, and pdoom-data then supplies that. Direction of authority is pdoom1 -> pdoom-data. So this issue carries measurements and questions, and deliberately **no proposal**.

Findings come from a read-only static audit of this repo plus JSON measurement of the corpus. The game was not run; anything runtime-dependent is flagged.

---

## The question

**What do you actually want a pdoom-data event to carry?**

Everything below exists so that can be answered against facts rather than against either side's guesses. If the answer is "much less than we currently send", that is a good outcome and cheap to deliver.

---

## What pdoom1 reads today

`godot/data/historical_events.json`, 1,194 records. Every raw-record access in the tree is in one file, `godot/autoload/event_service.gd`.

**Nine of thirteen fields are read.** Never accessed anywhere: `sources` (1,194 records, none empty), `tags`, `impacts[].condition` (3,636 entries, all null), `source_id`. `pdoom_impact` is copied onto the transformed event and then read by nothing; 1,187 of its 1,194 values are null.

Derived keys written onto the game event that nothing downstream reads: `eligibility_start`, `eligibility_end`, `trigger_mode`, `historical`, `significance`, `source_data` (which carries a full copy of the raw record).

## The number that should shape the answer

**98.3% of the corpus never reaches a decision window.** `_is_flavour_event` (`event_service.gd:491-497`) demotes every `technical_research_breakthrough` and every `arxiv*` id to `delivery_tier: "feed"`. Feed items render as one grey line and **their options are never presented and their effects never applied**.

1,174 of 1,194 records are inert beyond `id`, `title`, `category`, `year`. Twenty can open a window; one is then dropped by the start-year filter.

**So the decision surface pdoom1 gets from 1,194 curated events is nineteen records.**

That is the single most decision-relevant fact in this audit. If pdoom-data is supplying 1,194 records to fill nineteen slots, the contract question is not "which fields" but "which records, and chosen how".

## Rarity is not carrying the meaning your curve file assumes

Corpus: rare 1,076, common 77, legendary 41.

**All 41 `legendary` records are in the arxiv/flavour stream** — so the tier meaning "always fires at its historical date, key story beat" is applied exclusively to records that are then demoted to a grey line. The nineteen records that can open a window are seventeen `common` and three `rare`. **Zero legendary.**

Cause, measured in pdoom-data: `rarity` is an exact `text_length > 20000` threshold on a field that is not carried into the output (`pdoom-data#51`). Zero violations in 1,129 records. Correlation with the visible description length is r = -0.0065.

Boundary case nobody validates: `_get_rarity_settings` tests `_rarity_curves.has(rarity)`, and `rarity_curves.json` has top-level keys `default_rarity`, `year_trigger`, `_description`, `_note`. A record with `rarity: "year_trigger"` would pass that test and return the wrong dict. No such record exists today.

## Significance discriminates almost nothing

`significance` is summed from `abs(change)` across `impacts` and scales every generated option's effects (`event_service.gd:500-528`, `:587-590`).

**1,166 of 1,194 records score exactly 6.** Whole-corpus distribution `{6: 1166, 8: 4, 9: 6, 10: 18}`.

## `impacts` are not inert, and three of your docs say they are

`events.gd:290-310` intercepts a literal `doom` key and reroutes it into `doom_system.add_stream_input("panic", ...)`. Its own comment names **pdoom-data-derived events as the sole remaining producer of literal doom effects**.

`WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP.md:280-282`, `TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md:78-79` and `resource_accessor.gd:73-76` all still describe that path as an inert sink. Flagging as a doc/code disagreement rather than asserting which is intended.

Meanwhile pdoom-data's supplied vocabulary — `vibey_doom`, `stress`, `burnout_risk` — maps onto `doom` via `variable_mapping.json`, which is precisely what ADR-0015 outlaws. It survives only because of that reroute. Three variables are silently dropped as unmapped: `ethics_risk` (16), `technical_debt` (12), `media_reputation` (4). They still count toward significance.

Path B (literal effects) reaches gameplay for **seven records only** — the `funding_catastrophe` branch. The other twelve window-tier records build effects from `significance` alone.

## Three asks already on your record that pdoom-data does not answer

Not new requests from us. These are pdoom1's own documents.

**ADR-0012** (accepted 2026-07-12) names four event-content fields: *class, expiry N, response-expected flag, carrying-cost hook*. pdoom-data supplies none; everything defaults to `deferrable`.

**pdoom1#630 / `UI_FEATURES_STACK.md:39-44`** — the feed drowning in `hist_arxiv`, "the ENTIRE hist_arxiv deck fires, 200+ entries in event_cooldowns". `SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-17.md:36-37` names pdoom-data's salience tiers as the principled fix. pdoom-data has that field on its candidate feed (`salience_tier_by_profile`, A 172 / B 687 / C 1717 / D 858) but **not on `all_events.json`**, which is the collection you read.

**`TRIUMVIRATE_METABOLIC_CYCLE.md:90-116`** (proposed, not ratified) asks for monthly facts-only packs and states the split: *pdoom-data owns the fact schema, pdoom1 owns the shaping schema*. pdoom-data has since ratified its side of that as ADR-007 and ADR-008.

## One thing pdoom-data will not do, and why it is in your interest

DQ-21 is resolved and its vocabulary is live — `general_capability`, `frontier_capability`, `global_compute`, `dedicated_ai_compute`, `political_pressure`, `ambient_risk`, `global_alarm`, `global_panic`, accepted at `events.gd:315-337`. pdoom-data could encode those names directly.

**ADR-007 in pdoom-data says it should not**, and the reason favours you: if we encode `frontier_capability` and you later rename or split it, every exported pack already in the wild silently means the wrong thing — no error, no failed parse, just numbers attached to a concept that no longer exists. An external taxonomy plus a mapping table on your side keeps your vocabulary yours to revise as often as the design needs.

If you would rather have your names directly, say so and we will do it — but that is the trade being made.

## Also outstanding, unrelated to schema

`pdoom1#1098` — 42 records in the bundled copy still carry un-redacted email addresses. `scripts/sync_from_pdoom_data.sh` reads directories that no longer exist in pdoom-data and has never successfully run, so there is no path for upstream corrections to arrive.

## Could not determine

Whether any of this holds at runtime; everything is static tracing plus JSON measurement. Why `historical_events.json` is a hand-commit rather than a sync output. Whether the "inert sink" docs are simply stale post-#985 or describe a path not traced.

Refs `pdoom-data#43`, `pdoom-data#51`, `pdoom-data#52`, `pdoom-data#55`, `pdoom1#630`, `pdoom1#1052`, `pdoom1#1098`, `pdoom1-website#240`.

issues.title: docs: ladder epoch columns are off by one from v0.14 down in ROADMAP.md and RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md
issues.body:
Extracted from #1018 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. Verified live on `main` at 2026-08-06.

## The defect

Two published documents map version to ladder epoch, and both are off by one from v0.14 down:

- `docs/ROADMAP.md:47` -- `| v0.14 | Aug 7 | L3 | Per-tick & People (prov.) | ... |`
- `docs/RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md:89` -- `| **Aug 7** | **Fri** | **Theme v0.14 ...** | Epoch+Seed | 0.14 / **L3** | **Yes** |`

L3 was spent mid-month by #982 and the shipped build is already `0.13.2 / L3`. So `v0.14 -> L3` claims the next epoch will NOT fork the ladder, when by both documents' own rules it must. Every row below inherits the shift (`v0.15 -> L4` should be L5, and so on).

## Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

The ladder epoch is the board key. `tools/sync_version.py --check` gates pre-commit and CI precisely because a silent version drift forks the leaderboard -- CLAUDE.md calls that fatal. These two tables are the human-readable half of the same contract, and they currently disagree with the shipped constant. Anyone planning the Aug 7 cut from either table plans the wrong board.

Cheap: two table columns, plus a scan for other places the mapping is restated.

## Provenance

Found by the #1018 ADR-supersession scan on 2026-07-29 and recorded there as one of six collisions. #1018 is being closed and folded into #1049; #1049 is a broader ADR-honesty issue raised from the website side and does **not** carry the collision matrix. This one is live, so it is filed separately rather than left in a folded issue.

One of the six has since self-resolved: the stale `game_config.gd:159-160` runtime comment ("Epoch L1 == the current ruleset", above a const reading `"3"`) is gone from `main`.

## Adjacent, from the same scan, if someone is in these files anyway

`L<n>` is overloaded: ladder epochs L1/L2/L3 versus the distribution update ladder L0-L3. Same notation, unrelated meanings, both spoken in league week. #1018 asked for that namespace to be ruled. Worth one sentence in `RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md` disambiguating them.

Source: #1018 (closing). Related: #1049 (the broader ADR pass), #982, `docs/GLOSSARY.md`.

issues.title: events: four measured defects in the pdoom-data ingest path (rarity boundary case, dropped-but-counted variables, inert-sink doc disagreement, constant significance)
issues.body:
Extracted from #1102 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`.

#1102 is a measured, read-only audit of what pdoom1 gets from pdoom-data, and its headline question was answered by the memo at `docs/memos/MEMO_2026-08-04_1106-and-1102.html`. But #1102 is memo-shaped, and four **code-level defects in THIS repo** are buried inside it. The memo carries the headline numbers (1,194 records / nineteen decision records / rarity / significance) and does not carry these. They are measurements, so re-deriving them means redoing the audit.

None of these were run against a live game -- #1102 states everything is static tracing plus JSON measurement. Treat each as "verify, then fix", not "fix".

## 1. `_get_rarity_settings` has a boundary case that returns the wrong dict

`_get_rarity_settings` tests `_rarity_curves.has(rarity)`. `rarity_curves.json` has top-level keys `default_rarity`, `year_trigger`, `_description`, `_note`. **A record with `rarity: "year_trigger"` would pass that test and be handed a configuration dict that is not a rarity curve.** No such record exists in the corpus today, so this is latent, not live -- but the corpus is externally supplied and the check is a `has()` against a dict that mixes data with metadata.

Fix shape: validate against an explicit allowlist of rarity names, not against key presence in a file that also holds `_description`.

## 2. Three supplied variables are silently dropped but still inflate `significance`

`ethics_risk` (16 records), `technical_debt` (12), `media_reputation` (4) arrive in `impacts` and are dropped as unmapped -- **and still count toward the `significance` sum**, which scales every generated option's effect magnitude (`event_service.gd:500-528`, `:587-590`).

So an event whose only impacts are unmapped variables produces a larger effect than an event with no impacts, for no reason a designer could see. Silent, and it moves numbers.

Fix shape: decide whether unmapped variables should map, be rejected loudly at load, or be excluded from the significance sum. Any of the three beats the current behaviour.

## 3. Three documents describe an active code path as an inert sink

`events.gd:290-310` intercepts a literal `doom` key in `impacts` and reroutes it into `doom_system.add_stream_input("panic", ...)`. Its own comment names pdoom-data-derived events as the sole remaining producer of literal doom effects.

These three all still say that path is dead:
- `WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP.md:280-282`
- `TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md:78-79`
- `resource_accessor.gd:73-76`

#1102 flagged this as a doc/code disagreement without asserting which is intended. Someone has to rule. Note the ADR-0015 angle: pdoom-data's `vibey_doom` / `stress` / `burnout_risk` map onto `doom` via `variable_mapping.json`, which is precisely what ADR-0015 outlaws, and the mapping survives ONLY because of that reroute. So "which document is right" is really "is ADR-0015 being honoured here".

## 4. `significance` discriminates almost nothing

**1,166 of 1,194 records score exactly 6.** Whole-corpus distribution `{6: 1166, 8: 4, 9: 6, 10: 18}`. It is used as a scaling multiplier on option effects, so in practice it is a constant with 28 exceptions. Either it should carry meaning or it should stop being a multiplier -- but it should not silently be a constant wearing the costume of a signal.

Related: the same section of #1102 measures that **all 41 `legendary` records are in the demoted arxiv/flavour stream**, so the tier meaning "always fires at its historical date, key story beat" is applied exclusively to records rendered as one grey line. The nineteen records that can open a decision window are seventeen `common` and three `rare`. **Zero legendary.** That is a content-authoring fact worth knowing before anyone tunes rarity.

## Also worth carrying forward

pdoom-data has `salience_tier_by_profile` on its candidate feed (A 172 / B 687 / C 1717 / D 858) but **not on `all_events.json`**, which is the collection pdoom1 reads. `SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-17.md:36-37` names salience tiers as the principled fix for the feed drowning in `hist_arxiv` (#630). The field exists upstream and is not on the surface we consume.

Source: #1102 (closing; headline answered by the 08-04 memo). Refs `pdoom-data#43`, `#51`, `#52`, `#55`, `pdoom1#630`, `#1052`, `#1098`.

issues.title: content: promote the real-people/real-venue content guardrail from a closing issue comment to a tracked doc
issues.body:
Extracted from #803 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. #803 (revisit ADR-0014 conferences) is being retired because its days-granularity premise was overtaken by the turn=ONE MONTH ruling (#1125). But its comment thread carries a content-safety ruling that has nothing to do with conference granularity, is not recorded in any document, and applies to a large and growing amount of generated content.

`grep -rln "real named|wrongdoing|fictional venue" docs/` returns nothing on `main` at 2026-08-06. This ruling exists in exactly one place: a GitHub comment on an issue about to be closed.

## The ruling (Pip, 2026-07-22, verbatim)

> **Governing principle:** NEVER imply wrongdoing by a single real human, or realistic institutional negligence by a real named entity, in any period between sim-start and modern day. Historical contributions to AI capabilities are NOT morally judged -- only PLAYER and RIVAL actions carry moral weight.

> **The differential (solved by simple writing):** a mishap is fine when it is distinctively WEIRD / fantastical (clearly not a realistic real-world failing); NOT fine when it reads as plausible real-world negligence or wrongdoing attributable to the real named venue/person.

> - OK: ninjas rappel through the ceiling and steal a briefcase.
> - OK: the return flight is delayed by a doomstorm.
> - NOT OK: a conference volunteer pickpockets an attendee in line (implies the real event had thieving staff).
> - NOT OK: the venue roof leaks from poor maintenance (implies real venue negligence).

> **Easter eggs:** fictional-researcher vignettes are the sweet spot -- e.g. a low-impulse-control researcher returns 2 days late "worse for wear and glazed", minus their Settlers of Catan, plus a USB of bitcoin they cannot remember.

And the accepted pushback recorded in the same comment, applying Pip's own rule back to a suggestion of his:

> keep such pegs FICTIONAL. Naming a real recent person (e.g. a real convicted financier) reintroduces exactly the real-human-wrongdoing risk the rule forbids -- even as a joke, even about someone with real convictions. Keep the vignette; drop the real name. The fictional researcher is funnier AND zero-risk.

## Why this needs a home

The game ships 1,194 historical records naming real people and real organisations, wants conference data populated from real events, and has a stated intent to generate flavour, antagonists, scandals and travel mishaps on top of that. The rule is the thing standing between "juicy flavour" and a defamation-shaped problem, and right now the only way to learn it is to have been in the thread.

It also generalises past conferences: it is really a rule about the boundary between the historical corpus (neutral, unjudged) and the fictional layer (where moral weight lives).

## Ask

Promote it to a tracked doc -- `docs/game-design/CONTENT_SAFETY_RULES.md` or a section in `DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY.md`, whichever Pip prefers -- keeping the four worked examples, because the examples are what make the differential usable by someone writing copy at speed. Cross-reference it from wherever event/flavour content gets authored, and from the pdoom-data contract if real-entity records flow in from there.

Source: #803 (closing as overtaken). Related: ADR-0014, #1102 (the pdoom-data corpus), DQ-16.

issues.title: ui(input): sweep the '_input shortcut + focused Control' double-fire shape across godot/scripts/ui
issues.body:
Extracted from #1032 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. PR #1144 fixed `config_confirmation.gd`. #1032 explicitly declined to scope the sweep, and said why:

> Wider point worth a moment's thought rather than a rule: this file is one of several that hand-roll `_input` keyboard shortcuts alongside a focused control. The same "shortcut handler plus focused button" shape exists elsewhere in `godot/scripts/ui/` and each instance needs the same discipline. Not proposing a sweep in this issue; noting that **the shape is the bug, not the file.**

## The mechanism, restated

A script handles a key in `_input()` and does not call `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()`. A Godot `Button` that holds focus activates on the `ui_accept` action, which ENTER is bound to by default. The same keypress therefore reaches BOTH paths and the handler runs twice.

In `config_confirmation.gd` the observable damage was `GameConfig.increment_games_played()` running twice per keyboard launch -- so the statistic was inflated ~2x for keyboard players and 1x for mouse players, incoherent across the population rather than merely wrong by a constant. That is the interesting part: the consequence was not the double navigation (absorbed by `SceneTransition`'s guard) but a quietly corrupted counter that nothing would ever flag.

## Ask

1. Enumerate every `_input` / `_gui_input` handler under `godot/scripts/ui/` that responds to ENTER, SPACE, or ESC while a Control in the same scene can hold focus.
2. For each: decide whether the double-fire is harmless (no competing handler wired) or damaging (a side effect that is not idempotent), and mark the event handled either way.
3. Look specifically for non-idempotent side effects -- counters, appends, submissions, persisted config writes -- because those are the ones that fail silently.

Not urgent. Worth doing as one pass rather than one bug at a time, because the second instance will present as a different symptom entirely.

Source: #1032 (closing, first instance fixed in PR #1144). Related: #1027 (silent wrongness), #1120 (keyboard/navigation surface -- coordinate before touching input handling).

issues.title: core: pending_events is an unguarded public queue -- give it one validated entry point (class fix behind #1134)
issues.body:
Extracted from #1134 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. PR #1144 fixed the instance -- F3 event injection now refuses outside `ACTION_SELECTION`, with a legible refusal and an exhaustive phase test. This is the class fix that #1134 flagged and deliberately left out of scope.

## #1134's own words

> The deeper version, worth considering separately: `pending_events` is a queue any caller can push to with no validation. This is the first caller found doing it wrongly; it is unlikely to be the last. A single guarded entry point would make the class impossible rather than this instance.

## The shape of the problem

`gm.state.pending_events.append(event)` is a raw array append on a public field. The invariant that matters -- an event may only be enqueued in a phase that will drain it -- currently lives in ONE caller (`debug_overlay.gd`, after #1144). Any other caller, present or future, gets no help. The failure mode when it goes wrong is not an error: it is a run that cannot advance, which is the worst-behaved outcome in this codebase's taxonomy (see #1027).

## Ask

Route all enqueues through a single named method on GameState or GameManager that:

1. checks the current phase can drain the queue, and refuses otherwise;
2. returns a result the caller can act on rather than failing silently;
3. names explicitly any phases that may legitimately accept an event for LATER draining, if such phases exist.

Then make `pending_events` unreachable for direct append from outside (or, if GDScript makes that awkward, add a test that greps for `pending_events.append` outside the guarded module -- the repo already uses that pattern for scene navigation via `tools/check_scene_nav.py`).

## Scope note

Worth checking at the same time whether other queue-shaped fields on GameState have the same exposure. The generator here is "a public array that a state machine drains", not "events specifically".

Source: #1134 (closing, instance fixed in PR #1144). Related: #1027, #1112 (dev-tool versus alpha-tool boundary).

issues.title: release: add a BEHAVIOURAL build-identity check to the release checklist (a feature the old build cannot have)
issues.body:
Extracted from #1067 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. #1067's headline defect (CI shipped a stale `build_stamp.txt`) IS fixed -- CI exports route through `tools/build_release.py` now. This is the "bonus" half of that issue, which was never actioned and is not recorded anywhere else.

## The observation, verbatim from #1067

> Build identity was confirmed in about fifteen seconds behaviourally -- open the scenario dropdown, see the amber `[!] NOT RANKED` warning that only exists in code merged at 16:15 that day. **A feature that cannot exist in the previous version is a stronger identity check than any string the build prints about itself.** Worth writing into the release checklist regardless of whether the stamp gets fixed.

## Why it is worth a ticket

The stamp is a string the artifact prints ABOUT itself. It cannot fail loudly -- when wrong it reports a plausible commit on a plausible date, which is exactly how it sent someone three weeks in the wrong direction on 2026-07-31. Every fix to the stamp is a fix to a self-report. A behavioural check is orthogonal evidence: it cannot be faked by a stale file, a stale cache, or a wrong upload, because the feature either exists in the running binary or it does not.

## Verified absent

`grep -niE "NOT RANKED|behaviour|behavior|feature that cannot exist|identity" .github/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` returns nothing on `main` at 2026-08-06.

## Ask

Add a step to `.github/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`:

- Before announcing a release, name one feature that CANNOT exist in the previous version, launch the downloaded artifact, and observe it.
- The step should require naming the feature at cut time (it changes every release), not point at a fixed thing.
- Keep the stamp check too -- this is a second, independent line, not a replacement.

Small. The value is that it makes the identity check a habit rather than a thing someone improvises when suspicious.

Source: #1067 (closing). Family: `docs/POSTMORTEM_2026-07-31_LEAGUE_DAY.md`, #1027.
